trusted: The coordinator invokes the reviewed bootstrap template with exact reviewed substitutions.
Git object bytes are content-addressed and read with GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1.
The pinned host executables match their SHA-256 values.
The local Docker daemon and digest-bound image report truthful inspect and cgroup state.
The three multi-agent receipt artifacts are trusted-local review attestations after exact schema validation.
excluded: A malicious concurrent process under the same uid after bootstrap begins.
Intentional Git object-store corruption, branch reset, reflog deletion, or history rewrite after the consumption commit.
Compromise of the Docker daemon, host kernel, SHA-256 implementation, or pinned executables.
Power loss or host loss; these produce an incomplete infrastructure result if the run directory or consumption commit exists without a complete receipt.
model.limitation: The committed consumption marker is durable under the trusted no-history-rewrite model. It is not an append-only guarantee against a malicious same-uid repository owner.

rules: The reviewed protocol commit P is clean and has exactly one parent equal to expected_parent_commit_sha1.
The recursive raw Git delta from the parent is expected_delta exactly.
All four files are regular Git blobs at mode 100644 and match their bound SHA-256 values.
Every receipt copies the byte-identical protocol and all three executable-policy hashes.
The bootstrap disables replacement objects and verifies P parent, raw modes/paths, protocol hash, and all runner/policy hashes before any runner byte executes.
A has sole parent P and exactly the four review/decision blobs.
The hash-bound authorization validator enforces exact keys, JSON types, role IDs, principal freshness, raw deltas, trees, inventories, authority bits, and receipt blob hashes.
Before any Docker container is created, the host runner atomically claims the run directory and commits C with sole parent A and exactly the one marker blob.
Every later Git archive is addressed by exact C with replacement objects disabled.
Current HEAD no longer equals A after C, so canonical replay fails even if the untracked run directory is removed.

canonical_bootstrap.runner_script_template:
set -u
umask 077
export GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1
repo='/Volumes/Volume/crypto-autoresearcher-worktrees/recursive-s3-quotient-001'
branch='refs/heads/codex/recursive-s3-quotient-001'
base='c2048512ae6d151e532eff41bfd13de5a77316da'
p='@PROTOCOL_COMMIT_SHA1@'
protocol_sha='@PROTOCOL_SHA256@'
host_sha='@HOST_RUNNER_SHA256@'
validator_sha='@AUTHORIZATION_VALIDATOR_SHA256@'
container_sha='@CONTAINER_RUNNER_SHA256@'
exp='experiments/EXP-SGCP-SECANT-REP-001'
protocol_path="${exp}/development-test-execution-protocol-v3.json"
host_path="${exp}/development-test-host-runner-v3.zsh"
validator_path="${exp}/development-test-authorization-validator-v3.jq"
container_path="${exp}/development-test-container-runner-v3.py"
source_path="${exp}/src/sgcp_secant_math_core.py"
test_path="${exp}/tests/test_sgcp_secant_math_core.py"
accounting_path="${exp}/development-test-accounting-review-v3.json"
decision_path="${exp}/development-test-decision-v3.json"
red_path="${exp}/development-test-red-team-review-v3.json"
theory_path="${exp}/development-test-theory-review-v3.json"
sha_path() { /usr/bin/env -i HOME=/tmp TMPDIR=/tmp LANG=C LC_ALL=C PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 /usr/bin/git -C "$repo" show "${1}:${2}" | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'; }
raw_delta() { /usr/bin/env -i HOME=/tmp TMPDIR=/tmp LANG=C LC_ALL=C PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 /usr/bin/git -C "$repo" diff-tree --raw --no-abbrev --no-commit-id -r "$1" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1, $2, $5, $6}'; }
[[ "$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 /usr/bin/git | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')" == '44a68ddc1983d6cff3fd35ba3f9ba5f82004216f1dcde69892b3d1b06e408698' ]] || exit 72
[[ "$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 /bin/zsh | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')" == '528da649cc69510bd3c0bc565298cb602076b74a8ac3f18e793211b2a3c725e8' ]] || exit 72
a=$(/usr/bin/env -i HOME=/tmp TMPDIR=/tmp LANG=C LC_ALL=C PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 /usr/bin/git -C "$repo" rev-parse HEAD) || exit 72
[[ "$(/usr/bin/env -i HOME=/tmp TMPDIR=/tmp LANG=C LC_ALL=C PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 /usr/bin/git -C "$repo" symbolic-ref -q HEAD)" == "$branch" ]] || exit 72
[[ -z "$(/usr/bin/env -i HOME=/tmp TMPDIR=/tmp LANG=C LC_ALL=C PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 /usr/bin/git -C "$repo" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all)" ]] || exit 72
[[ -z "$(/usr/bin/env -i HOME=/tmp TMPDIR=/tmp LANG=C LC_ALL=C PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 /usr/bin/git -C "$repo" replace -l)" ]] || exit 72
grafts=$(/usr/bin/env -i HOME=/tmp TMPDIR=/tmp LANG=C LC_ALL=C PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 /usr/bin/git -C "$repo" rev-parse --git-path info/grafts) || exit 72
[[ ! -e "$grafts" ]] || exit 72
[[ "$(/usr/bin/env -i HOME=/tmp TMPDIR=/tmp LANG=C LC_ALL=C PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 /usr/bin/git -C "$repo" rev-list --parents -n 1 "$p")" == "${p} ${base}" ]] || exit 72
[[ "$(/usr/bin/env -i HOME=/tmp TMPDIR=/tmp LANG=C LC_ALL=C PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 /usr/bin/git -C "$repo" rev-list --parents -n 1 "$a")" == "${a} ${p}" ]] || exit 72
[[ "$(raw_delta "$p")" == ":000000 100644 A ${validator_path}"$'\n'":000000 100644 A ${container_path}"$'\n'":000000 100644 A ${protocol_path}"$'\n'":000000 100644 A ${host_path}" ]] || exit 72
[[ "$(raw_delta "$a")" == ":000000 100644 A ${accounting_path}"$'\n'":000000 100644 A ${decision_path}"$'\n'":000000 100644 A ${red_path}"$'\n'":000000 100644 A ${theory_path}" ]] || exit 72
[[ "$(sha_path "$p" "$protocol_path")" == "$protocol_sha" ]] || exit 72
[[ "$(sha_path "$p" "$host_path")" == "$host_sha" ]] || exit 72
[[ "$(sha_path "$p" "$validator_path")" == "$validator_sha" ]] || exit 72
[[ "$(sha_path "$p" "$container_path")" == "$container_sha" ]] || exit 72
[[ "$(sha_path "$a" "$source_path")" == '8b8781d688188afa41e87f33e15a306fc5a9f5326b8e93316247263ee8f933bd' ]] || exit 72
[[ "$(sha_path "$a" "$test_path")" == '2b0e34524f22cf5d2dd70c3eff857b186c10c9d8882bb2893999febc1352417a' ]] || exit 72
/usr/bin/env -i HOME=/tmp TMPDIR=/tmp LANG=C LC_ALL=C PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin DOCKER_HOST=unix:///var/run/docker.sock GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 /usr/bin/git -C "$repo" show "${a}:${host_path}" | /usr/bin/env -i HOME=/tmp TMPDIR=/tmp LANG=C LC_ALL=C PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin DOCKER_HOST=unix:///var/run/docker.sock GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 /bin/zsh -f -s -- launch "$a" "$p" "$protocol_sha" "$host_sha" "$validator_sha" "$container_sha"
status="${pipestatus[2]}"
exit "$status"
canonical_bootstrap.instantiation_rule: After P is committed and all three GO receipts are validated into A, replace every template token once with the exact lowercase hexadecimal value bound by A. Reject any remaining token, extra substitution, prefix, suffix, alternate cwd, environment, or argv.
canonical_bootstrap.trust_order: The instantiated bootstrap verifies Git topology/raw modes and SHA-256 of the exact host runner blob before streaming that blob to zsh. No repository runner byte executes earlier.

rules: Before authorization, the complete sorted sidecar/cache inventories and ancestor list are empty.
The host runner repeats fail-closed complete experiment-scope inventories before claim, immediately before Docker creation, and after cleanup.
Every find command status is checked; an unreadable path is infrastructure failure.
The run-directory sibling sidecar remains absent.

host_runner.atomic_claim: Direct mkdir without -p claims the run path after all immutable preclaim checks.
host_runner.durable_consumption: Before Docker create, a hooks-disabled, unsigned, exact-path Git commit C adds only the canonical consumption marker. C has sole parent A and sets maximum_runs_remaining to zero.

host_output_limit.scope: The shell that runs Git archive, tee, Docker attach, stdout/stderr, timeout diagnostics, and resource accounting inherits RLIMIT_FSIZE. Trusted bounded setup receipts are outside this limit.

wall_limit.rule: Timeout diagnostics are separated from untrusted container stderr and require both GNU-timeout status and its fixed diagnostic prefix.

resource_accounting.host: time -lp covers the bounded Git-archive/tee/Docker-attach pipeline.
resource_accounting.container: The canonical JSON contains before/after cgroup CPU, memory current/peak, and pids current/peak counters.
resource_accounting.limits: Container preflight verifies cgroup memory, swap, CPU and pids plus RLIMIT_NOFILE, RLIMIT_FSIZE, root read-only, and tmpfs/shm mount properties.
resource_accounting.limitation: Host setup and final receipt costs are retained as fixed development overhead but are not included in the pipeline time receipt.

input_transport.method: git archive at exact C, piped through tee to Docker stdin
input_transport.rule: The digest-bound image extracts into capped /tmp, verifies the container-runner SHA-256 before Python starts, and the runner verifies source/test hashes before import.

host_runner.one_shot_rule: Run-directory creation consumes the immediate attempt; C durably consumes authorization before protected execution. Existing C or non-A HEAD rejects replay. Missing receipt after claim or C is INCOMPLETE_INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE.

receipt_format.terminal_rule: Every normal terminal path after claim writes classification and the complete receipt. Existing claim/C without a complete receipt is classified post hoc as INCOMPLETE_INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE.

container.creation: docker create returns an unnamed 64-hex container ID; all inspect/start/removal operations use that exact ID only.
container.ownership: Before start and before removal, inspect must show exact ID plus authorization and consumption labels. No name-based inspect or removal exists.
container.cleanup_rule: VALID_DEVELOPMENT_TEST requires valid post-run inspect, OOMKilled=false, exact exited state, successful rm -f by verified ID, reachable pinned Docker server, and subsequent inspect failure proving absence.

canonical_test_result.validator_rule: Slurp exactly one JSON value; require one LF-terminated line, exact canonical jq -cS bytes, exact keys/types/events/counters, empty details, empty stderr, monotone bounded cgroup metrics, exit/status agreement, OOM false, and mandatory cleanup.
canonical_test_result.interpretation: A valid result is development evidence for the exact public-core behavior only. It is not an experiment run, curve-family result, relation-generation result, scaling estimate, rho comparison, or ECDLP improvement.

rules: Each GO receipt has exact keys and exact role ID/path.
Every reviewer ID is a UUID string, fresh, outside the 39 exclusions, and pairwise distinct.
Every observed topology/tree/raw delta/mode/hash/image/inventory fact is exact.
Any defect produces REVISE and no GO JSON.

authorization_decision_schema.required_interpretation: One isolated public development-test run only; no registered seed, campaign, experiment, scaling, rho, or ECDLP-improvement authority.
rules: The coordinator writes the decision only after three exact GO receipts.
Receipt hashes and role-to-principal maps equal the committed blobs exactly.
All identities/digests equal P and the protected source/test.
The decision grants exactly one development run and no cryptanalytic experiment authority.

theory: Does the stream-extracted runner load exactly the five bound tests and no alternate input?
Are Python startup, import origin, cgroup/mount preflight, and development-only interpretation exact?
Is the explicit trusted-local model stated narrowly enough?
accounting: Does C consume authorization before protected execution and resist ordinary replay?
Are host output, wall time, Docker HostConfig, cgroup usage, OOM, inspect, and cleanup evidence complete for the stated model?
Can every terminal and incomplete outcome be distinguished without overclaim?
red_team: Can any unverified runner byte execute, any schema/type forgery pass, or any replacement/graft/raw-mode substitution survive?
Can mutable paths, container naming, extra JSON values/keys, stderr, timeout text, failed inspect/cleanup, sidecars, caches, or output flooding false-pass?
Does the stated no-malicious-concurrent-writer/no-history-rewrite boundary honestly contain remaining TOCTOU and replay limits?

go_no_go.go: Three fresh exact GO receipts, a validated four-file A commit directly on P, exact bootstrap instantiation, clean inventories, absent run/marker, pinned tools/image, and no replacement/graft state.
go_no_go.no_go: Any REVISE, mismatch, remaining token, inventory/cache, tool/image drift, existing run/marker, dirty tree, replacement/graft, or inability to preserve C and all outcomes leaves execution unauthorized.
go_no_go.next_action_after_go: Invoke the exact instantiated bootstrap once. Preserve C and the complete run directory, then obtain independent result interpretation before any experiment design.
